# BENCH-01 — Checkout Incident Investigation Report

## Decision

**The root cause is a nil-pointer defect in coupon validation**, introduced by normalization change **N-42** in **build 842**. The database is ruled out as a contributing factor. The prescribed remediation is an immediate rollback from build 842 to build 841, with an expected recovery window of **four minutes**.

---

## Evidence

| Evidence ID | Source | Material Fact |
|---|---|---|
| **OBS-101** | bench-observer (telemetry & DB) | Checkout errors rose immediately after deployment of build 842. Database latency remained normal throughout the incident, ruling out a database-related cause. |
| **INV-111** | bench-investigator (logs & code) | Checkout application logs reveal a nil-pointer exception in the coupon validation path, traced directly to normalization change N-42, which was shipped in build 842. |
| **OPS-121** | bench-operator (remediation) | Safe rollback procedure: revert build 842 → build 841. Expected recovery time is four minutes. |

---

## Remediation

1. **Immediate action:** Roll back build 842 to the last known-good build, **build 841**. This will remove the defective normalization change N-42 from the checkout path.
2. **Expected recovery time:** Four minutes from initiation.
3. **Post-recovery:** The development team should correct the nil-pointer in coupon validation introduced by N-42 before any attempt to re-deploy the normalization change. A code review and pre-release test covering the coupon validation code path is strongly recommended prior to the next deployment.

cases.description: Diagnose and repair a fixed data-pipeline schema regression.

attempts.output:
All three specialists have returned their evidence. Here is the synthesized final report.

---

## Decision

The pipeline freshness regression was caused by an incompatible field rename introduced in schema release **S-19**. The field `tier` was renamed to `customer_tier`, but the downstream transform **T-31** was not updated to match. As a result, the parser rejected every record referencing the new field name, causing records to be dropped and the pipeline's end-to-end freshness to degrade from **8 minutes to 94 minutes** — a **10.75× regression**. The degradation began at deployment of S-19 and persisted until the mismatch is repaired.

---

## Evidence

| Evidence ID | Source | Material Fact |
|---|---|---|
| **OBS-404** | bench-observer | Pipeline freshness dropped from 8 minutes to 94 minutes after schema release S-19. |
| **INV-414** | bench-investigator | Parser logs reject the renamed field `customer_tier` because transform T-31 still expects `tier`. The incompatible field change is the rename of `tier` → `customer_tier` without a corresponding transform update. |
| **OPS-434** | bench-operator | The repair is to deploy transform T-32 with a `customer_tier` mapping, then replay all affected partitions starting from 06:00 UTC (the time of S-19 deployment). |

---

## Remediation

1. **Deploy transform T-32** — This transform maps the new field name `customer_tier` to the downstream consumers, replacing the broken T-31. The mapping must alias `customer_tier` appropriately so that all downstream logic expecting `tier` continues to function.

2. **Replay affected partitions** — Replay all partitions from 06:00 UTC onward (the time of S-19's deployment) to backfill the records that were rejected by T-31. This ensures no data loss from the regression window.

3. **Validate** — After replay, confirm that pipeline freshness returns to the pre-regression baseline of ≤8 minutes. Monitor parser logs to verify zero further rejections on the `customer_tier` field.

4. **Prevent recurrence** — Add a schema-compatibility gate that blocks schema releases when active transforms reference the old field name, preventing this class of mismatch from reaching production.
